Verdict: PASS — Stasis.
The stated goals of economic cooperation and mutual prosperity align directly with the structural actions of tariff elimination and bilateral investment.

Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi will make a historic visit to Auckland on July 10, marking the first visit by an Indian leader to New Zealand in four decades, following a major free trade agreement.

The Poison:
Rapid trade integration can create domestic market disruptions for specific local industries unable to compete with massive foreign export volumes.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
No major plane error detected. The diplomatic framing (WHY) matches the physical implementation of tariff reductions and bilateral investment commitments (WHERE/HOW).

Social Physics Analysis:
Both leaders act through social empowerment, aligning their stated intentions with transparent actions. By building a cooperative coalition, they reduce systemic economic strain and foster mutual growth.

The Trajectory: Stasis.
When stated intentions and actual outcomes align perfectly in the positive quadrant, the system maintains a stable trajectory within the Greater Good, expanding opportunities for both populations.

The Unavoidable Truth: True diplomatic progress is measured in lowered barriers and mutual economic integration, not just photo opportunities.

The Unavoidable Lie: That trade agreements benefit every single domestic sector equally without friction.
